description: Facts about the values of OpenFOAM's fvSchemes menus, each with its source: a statement of OpenFOAM's authors (kind header, a class Description; source, a quoted line of code; citation, a reference not checked by omniD), recorded as stated with its conditions, or omniD's own derivation, labelled kind derived. settled_by is null until a run of ours settles the claim. omniD reads none of it; the consumer that owns an attribute owns its schema.

conditions: the Euler coefficients apply while timeIndex < 2 (deltaT0_(vf) returns GREAT); timeIndex is the run's absolute time index, so a run restarted from a later index does not take them on its first step

stability.derivation: omniD's derivation, not a statement of OpenFOAM's authors: a linear decay rate acting on the old time level keeps the ddt operator stable while a = rate*deltaT stays below the bound; backward's characteristic polynomial 3z^2 + (2a - 4)z + 1 with |z| < 1 (Jury conditions) gives 4; see docs/solver-learning/cardiacfoam-pvj-coupling.md

stated_by.text: Second-order backward-differencing ddt using the current and two previous time-step values.

stated_by.excerpt: scalar backwardDdtScheme<Type>::deltaT0_(const GeoField& vf) const { if (mesh().time().timeIndex() < 2) { return GREAT; } else { return deltaT0_(); } }
stated_by.reading: deltaT0_(vf) is GREAT while timeIndex < 2, so those steps take the Euler coefficients

stability.derivation: omniD's derivation, not a statement of OpenFOAM's authors: a linear decay rate acting on the old time level keeps the ddt operator stable while a = rate*deltaT stays below the bound; Euler's amplification |1 - a| < 1 gives 2; see docs/solver-learning/cardiacfoam-pvj-coupling.md

stated_by.text: Basic first-order Euler implicit/explicit ddt using only the current and previous time-step values.

stated_by.reading: the time derivative is zero, so the scheme has no time order

conditions: the off-centring coefficient ocCoeff in [0,1] follows the name, or is given as a dictionary (a ramp function)
no formal order is stated for a coefficient below 1: the header states the second order only for a coefficient of 1, and Euler-implicit for 0

stated_by.text: Second-oder Crank-Nicolson implicit ddt using the current and previous time-step fields as well as the previous time-step ddt.
With a coefficient of 1 the scheme is fully centred and second-order, with a coefficient of 0 the scheme is equivalent to Euler-implicit.

conditions: steady-state computations with local time stepping only (the header says the scheme should only be used for those)

stated_by.text: Local time-step first-order Euler implicit/explicit ddt.

conditions: steady-state computations with local time stepping only (the header says the scheme should only be used for those)

stated_by.text: Courant number limited first-order Euler implicit/explicit ddt.

conditions: steady-state computations with local time stepping only (the header says the scheme should only be used for those)

stated_by.text: Stabilised local time-step first-order Euler implicit/explicit ddt.
Basic second-order gradient scheme using face-interpolation and Gauss' theorem.
A second-order gradient scheme using face-interpolation, Gauss' theorem and iterative skew correction.
Basic second-order laplacian using face-gradients and Gauss' theorem.
Basic second-order div using face-gradients and Gauss' theorem.
Basic second-order convection using face-gradients and Gauss' theorem.

conditions: the second order is the one the non-orthogonal correction restores; the header states the correction, not an order

stated_by.text: Surface gradient scheme with full explicit non-orthogonal correction.

stated_by.reading: the correction is built from the mesh's non-orthogonal correction vectors
